title: Raksha Mantri and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister perform Bhoomi Pujan for T-Series Tanks Overhaul Project at Vehicle Factory, Jabalpur
subtitle:
Rs 472 crore project to overhaul 80 tanks per annum, boosting Indian Army’s operational readiness, while generating employment opportunities
Nations with advanced technologies, resilient supply chains, robust industrial capacity, and dynamic innovation capabilities will be better equipped to withstand prolonged conflicts: Shri Rajnath Singh
body_text:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav performed the Bhoomi Pujan for T-Series Tanks Overhaul Project at Vehicle Factory, Jabalpur, a unit of Mini Ratna Defence Public Sector Undertaking Armoured Vehicles Nigam Limited (AVNL), on August 27, 2026. The project involves the creation of overhauling facilities for T-72 and T-90 Tanks with an estimated cost of Rs 472 crore, another milestone in the nation’s journey towards self-reliance.
The facilities at Vehicle Factory, Jabalpur have been envisaged to overhaul 80 tanks per annum to ensure timely availability of overhauled tanks to the Indian Army, further boosting its operational readiness. The Army requires 230 tanks to be overhauled each year, and the Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi, currently has the capacity to overhaul 150 tanks annually.
In his address, Raksha Mantri described the project as a testament to India’s growing technological prowess & industrial capabilities, expressing confidence that it would contribute to India’s goal of emerging as one of the world’s leading defence manufacturing and export hubs in the coming years. He emphasised that while the nature of warfare is changing with the advent of drones, precision-guided weapons, missiles, satellites, artificial intelligence and cyber warfare, the relevance of tanks has not diminished but evolved.
“Modern warfare demands combined capabilities rather than dependence on a single platform. Tanks, infantry, artillery, drones, air power, surveillance, and precision weapons together form an integrated combat system, a concept demonstrated by the Indian Army through its ‘Integrated Battle Group’. There is a need to equip our tanks with superior sensors and capabilities aligned with modern battlefield requirements. Our focus is to provide the soldiers with drones, missiles, artillery, electronic warfare capabilities, energy weapons & modernised tanks, and ensuring seamless coordination among them. This overhaul facility will advance this vision,” said Shri Rajnath Singh.
Raksha Mantri pointed out that the Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi, has supplied around 4,400 tanks to the Indian Army over the past four decades, reflecting its significant contribution to the country’s armoured capabilities. He said the new project will further strengthen Jabalpur’s identity as a major hub for defence technology, maintenance, modernisation and manufacturing. He expressed hope that AVNL, with 25 years of experience in overhauling T-72 and T-90 variant tanks, will set new benchmarks for quality, productivity, innovation, and global competitiveness in the years to come.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the Government's determined efforts towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat are transforming the country’s defence sector and the world’s perception of India. He stated that sustained efforts over the past decade have resulted in record increase in defence production to around Rs 1.80 lakh crore in Financial Year 2025-26 from Rs 46,000 crore in 2014, and all-time high defence exports of approximately Rs 39,000 crore from less than Rs 1,000 crore. He termed these milestones as a reflection of India’s emergence as a global manufacturing hub, a reliable technology partner and a trusted defence partner.
On the evolving nature of warfare, Raksha Mantri asserted that nations with advanced technologies, resilient supply chains, robust industrial capacity, and dynamic innovation capabilities will be better equipped to withstand prolonged conflicts. Against this backdrop, he stated that the Government is committed to ensuring that the defence forces are not dependent on foreign supply chains for critical requirements. “Our aim is to manufacture defence equipment domestically, undertake repair and maintenance within the country, upgrade existing systems with modern technologies, and develop next-generation capabilities indigenously,” he said.
The overhauling facilities for T-Series tanks will create significant opportunities for MSMEs by generating demand for a wide range of mechanical, electrical, electronic and hydraulic components, assemblies and subsystems. The sourcing of these items will help establish a robust and resilient supply chain, while creating avenues for local MSMEs in manufacturing and ancillary services associated with tank overhauling. This, in turn, will promote greater participation of local industry and contribute to the development of a strong and self-sustaining industrial ecosystem. Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the project would prove to be a boon for soldiers while generating employment opportunities for people in Jabalpur and surrounding areas, including farmers, workers, youth and small entrepreneurs.
Raksha Mantri commended the work being carried out by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in sectors such as industry, investment, and defence manufacturing with proactiveness and commitment. “Global Investors Summit 2025, the transparent and seamless approval system via 'Invest MP 3.0', and industry-friendly policies are establishing the state as an attractive hub for investment. The prospects for defence manufacturing on 3,073 hectares of land in the Gwalior-Chambal region and proposed investments exceeding Rs 16,960 crore reflect the state's vision. This effort is laying a strong foundation to make Madhya Pradesh India's next major Defence & Aerospace Manufacturing Hub,” he said.
Speaking on the occasion, Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav appreciated the investment being undertaken in Jabalpur, which will boost defence eco-system and encourage MSMEs participation in Madhya Pradesh. He credited the visionary leadership of PM Modi for India’s growing stature on the world stage, adding that the nation is prepared to tackle all kinds of challenges.
Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar; CMD, AVNL Shri Satyabrata Mukherjee and other senior officials of Department of Defence Production, AVNL and defence forces were present on the occasion.
